newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares rebound to end firmer.
newsitem.headline: KL shares rebound to end firmer.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur share prices rebounded from morning losses to end higher, with secondary issues recapturing interest after a spell of profit-taking.
"The Composite Index is very quiet," said an institutional dealer with a local securities firm. "Rotationally, some stocks are moving higher."

Finance sector stocks attracted some buyers, but other themes were absent. The blue chip-focused Composite Index rose 4.38 points to 1,237.50, while the Second Board index added 6.06 points to 612.60 after dipping to a low of 602.74 earlier.
Actively traded finance stocks included MBf Holdings, up three cents to 1.16 ringgit, Suria Capital, ahead seven cents to 2.35, and Rashid Hussain, up 90 cents to 17.90.
Volume at day's end stood at over 221 million shares, with the lion's portion of 154 million attributable to the main board.
"The market is still fairly quiet," said another institutional dealer. "There's no real direction to it."
Blue chip Tenaga traded up 30 cents to 12.20. A dealer said hopes for a rate hike helped lift the share price.
